body:
I played around with it some more.

I removed the `MultiplayerSynchronizer` on the bushes and used rpc to update the positions on the client instead.

I had three iterations of the code:
1. Iteration:
```gdscript
extends RigidBody2D

@rpc
func update_transform(transform: Transform2D) -> void:
	self.transform = transform
	# Also set linear and angular velocity here

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	if multiplayer.is_server(): 
		update_transform.rpc(transform)
```
This behaved so similar to the `MultiplayerSynchronizer` that I am pretty sure this is basically the implementation.

Meaning that the flickering was still there (and **very** noticeable)

2. Iteration:
```gdscript
extends RigidBody2D

var received_transform: Transform2D

@rpc
func update_transform(transform: Transform2D) -> void:
	received_transform = transform

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if multiplayer.is_server(): 
		update_transform.rpc(transform)
		return

	transform = received_transform
```
With this the flickering was gone!
But pushing the bushes around was a bit laggy now, since the position would only change when the server send the new one.

So I thought, "Let's update it only when new data comes, and in the mean time the client can handle the physics itself".
Kinda like client-side prediction, but not really.

The result:

3. Iteration:
```gdscript
extends RigidBody2D

var received_data: bool
var received_transform: Transform2D

@rpc
func update_transform(transform: Transform2D) -> void:
	received_transform = transform
	received_data = true

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if multiplayer.is_server(): 
		update_transform.rpc(transform)
		return
		
	if received_data:
		received_data = false
		transform = received_transform

```

Now the flicker was there again (even though not as strong as in the first iteration).
That makes me believe, that it is not the Multiplayer that makes this a problem, but maybe the physics engine? 
Because when I override the `Transform2D` every `_physics_process()` and thus practically disabling
the physics on the bush, it works.
But when I override it sometimes, it always flickers between where I set/teleport it, and where it was before.

The problem has nothing to do with the Multiplayer. When changing the the transform of a `RigidBody2D` the Collision shape does not seem to get moved.

After moving the `RigidBody2D` I can't collide with the node in the new place, but when I go to the old place I can collide with it, and it will snap back to there.

I have made a new demo:
[physics_desync.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21416001/physics_desync.zip)
[Demo Recording](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0709c07a-d85d-4553-bbcf-2df755a42979)

1. Store the player transform with the button (position is now marked)
2. Apply the transform to the Bush
3. Try collide with Bush (won't work)
4. Try to collide with Bush in the old position (marked)
-> Bush will snap back
5. Repeat

Since the nature of the bug has changed fundamentally, please let me now if I should change the Issue description or if this is now a duplicate.

It doesn't work because setting the transform does not set it in the Physics Server.
So you need to set it in the Physics Server instead.
```gdscript
func set_position_on_physics_body(body: RID, pos: Vector2D):
    PhysicsServer2D.body_set_state(
        body,
        PhysicsServer2D.BODY_STATE_TRANSFORM,
        Transform2D.IDENTITY.translated(pos),
    )

# Calling Example
set_position_on_physics_body($MyRigidBody2D, Vector2D.ZERO)
```
*(This was typed not copied, there might be typos)*

This is easily adaptable to 3D and Godot3, like described [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77721286/set-a-rigid-body-position-in-godot-4).

Alternatively, you can free your body and create a new one in the wanted position.

So now the Bug is: **Setting the transform of a Rigid Body does not update it in the Physics Server**.
Does it work if you use `_integrate_forces`? Directly assigning to the transform of Rigid bodies is not supported (as per the documentation)
